chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn al-Hussein al-Sa'd Abady narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from al-Hussein ibn Ali ibn Fadhal, from Ali ibn Aqbah, from Abu al-Jarud Ziyad ibn al-Munthir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The hardest of deeds are three: to be fair to people regarding yourself, so that you do not desire for them from yourself anything unless you desire for them the like of it; supporting your brother in wealth; and remembering God in every state. It is not merely saying 'Glory be to God, and praise be to God, and there is no god but God, and God is the Greatest', but rather when a command of God comes to you, you act upon it, and when something God has forbidden comes to you, you leave it.
ai.seo_question: What are the three hardest deeds for a believer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq highlights these three arduous duties as the pinnacle of spiritual discipline, emphasizing that true piety requires internalizing divine commands rather than limiting remembrance to mere verbal recitation. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on 'amal al-jawhari (substantive action) over 'amal al-lisani (verbal action), linking ethical conduct with people and financial generosity directly to one's obedience to God's will.
